headline: Sharks’ Igor Chernyshov out long term with injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that San Jose Sharks forward Igor Chernyshov will be out long term after leaving the game when a shot from Matinpalo struck his left arm.

It is a real loss for a team that is leaning on its goaltending. SJS sits at 6-4-1, but its share of expected goals, a measure of how the quality of chances split between the teams, is 44.4% so far this season. The Sharks are being outplayed and staying afloat because their goalies have saved 8.1 goals more than expected. Chernyshov was one of the few forwards moving the needle the other way. The Sharks' share of expected goals is 6.06 percentage points better with him on the ice, though his own 5-on-5 share is 47.92%. He has two goals against an expected 1.25, so some of his production was running a bit hot, but he scored 9 goals in 28 games last season and has held a regular role.

Going by how the coach has used his players, not games already played without him, Alexander Wennberg (20:21 a night) is next in line for Chernyshov's minutes, with the second power-play unit the other opening.
